source.title: Nonlinear Collaborative Scheme for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Hui-Ling Zhen; Xi Lin; Alan Tang; Zhenhua Li; Qing-Fu Zhang; S. Kwong

record.tranche_reason: Reports train and validation accuracy for standard single-loss CE training under partially randomized labels, using CIFAR-10 experiments rather than the original study’s full-random-labeling setup.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 reports accuracy curves at 20% and 80% label randomization for Residual Networks and Densenet. The text says accuracy decreases with randomization. Rows capture the standard single-loss CE results; the nonlinear and linear schemes are the study’s own alternative methods.
record.test_reason: The standard cross-entropy baselines train deep networks on randomly corrupted CIFAR-10 labels and measure training and validation accuracy, directly bearing on V4. The proposed loss comparisons are additional method evaluations.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the reported empirical conclusion: label randomization reduces training and validation accuracy, while the nonlinear collaborative scheme reportedly achieves higher accuracy and smoother curves than the single-loss and linear schemes.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes and evaluates a nonlinear collaborative loss, alongside single-loss CE and linear multi-loss comparisons; it does not reproduce the original study’s fully random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Label randomization level (20% versus 80%); network family (Residual Networks versus Densenet); dataset (CIFAR-10).

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report higher accuracy and smoother training curves for their nonlinear collaborative loss than for CE and linear loss combinations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed nonlinear loss improves accuracy and training stability under the tested clean-label and corrupted-label settings.

record.problems: Random-label results are shown only in Figure 3, without numerical values in the text. Only 20% and 80% randomization are reported; full random labeling is not shown. The text gives no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: Figure 3 gives accuracy curves without recoverable numerical values, and the text does not provide separate numeric outcomes. The result is summarized in the authors_conclusion and page excerpt instead.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error, chance test performance, and fitting without changing training hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
Shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, and Gaussian-noise inputs.

A complete corruption sweep through 100%, steady degradation across intermediate levels, and whether longer training eventually achieves perfect fitting. Regularization changes prevent a controlled comparison across all corruption conditions.
Controlled tests of whether explicit regularizers prevent memorization and whether removing them harms true-label generalization.
Separate learning trajectories for real and noisy labels. The spectral discussion does not establish their learning order.

record.verdict_notes: The relevant Figure 3 results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not listed as undeclared missing results. Exact curve values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied text. The study is not an original source for these versions.

versions.untested_parts: No completely random labeling result is stated.
Training time or convergence slowdown relative to true labels is not reported.
No unstructured input conditions are tested.

Only 20% and 80% randomization are shown, not a sweep from none to all. The text says train and validation accuracy decrease, but the figure-only curves do not establish perfect training accuracy or a steady rise in test error.
No test of whether regularization, dropout, or augmentation prevents fitting random labels, or whether removing it worsens true-label generalization.
No analysis of learning order or how real and random labels are learned over training.

relationships.condition: Standard CE training of Residual Networks and Densenet on CIFAR-10 at 20% and 80% label randomization, within the plotted training runs.
relationships.reason: Figure 3 and Section VII.B show reduced training and validation accuracy rather than perfect training fit in these runs. This qualifies V4 for the tested recipes and duration; regularization varies across some conditions. Based on the supplied text and figure axes; no row ids exist because these results were explicitly left out.
relationships.display_finding: Training and validation accuracy declined under corruption, with training fit remaining incomplete over the tested durations and regularization settings.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
